Title: Open Throat
Review:
This could’ve been great, but it lost me quickly and just did not land for me. Showing issues such as society’s disdain for the homeless and climate change is great, but it doesn’t feel like the author actually did anything with these themes. 

Also, This book should not have been marketed as queer. I get that we as queer people are othered and have to hide, and there’s a metaphor there with the lion’s life, but this felt like someone in a college creative writing class trying to be deep. The queerness was not overt enough to even really be recognizable.


I also wasn’t a huge fan of how little continuity there is in the sentience of the lion. It didn’t feel like there was any rhyme or reason to that, even metaphorically. I feel that Hoke should’ve committed to either making the lion fully anthropomorphized or not at all. It was just a very middle of the road book for me.
